sections.name: File setup, LockMode
sections.title: Rules and lock modes
sections.what: Explains the rules: a live call must be locked before the feed cutoff, historical moments are always allowed, and flags are only recorded. Also defines the two lock modes.
sections.why: Likely reason: records the rule for future readers.
sections.watch_out: Historical locks are always allowed, which is only safe if historical moments reveal nothing before a lock.

sections.name: lockAllowed, FlagCall, Flag
sections.title: Lock time check
sections.what: Allows a lock always for historical moments, and for live ones only when the server time is at or before the feed cutoff. Otherwise refuses with a plain reason. Throws an error if either time is not a valid timestamp.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops a fan locking after the outcome is visible in the feed.
sections.watch_out: It depends on the server clock. A wrong clock lets late locks through or refuses valid ones.

sections.name: BURST
sections.title: Flag thresholds
sections.what: Sets the limits: 10 locks within 60 seconds, 15 correct picks in a row, and 90 percent or more of at least 20 calls at 99 percent confidence.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The limits are fixed guesses, so ordinary fans could be flagged.

sections.name: anomalyFlags
sections.title: Unusual activity flags
sections.what: Checks the lock times for a burst, the longest run of correct picks, and near-maximum confidence. Adds a flag with a short description for each match. Flags are returned, not acted on.
sections.why: Likely reason: records patterns so a person can review them.
sections.watch_out: A lock time that cannot be read becomes an invalid number and can silently break the burst check.

summary: Basic checks on call timing and patterns: refuses live locks after the feed shows the ball was bowled, and flags unusual activity for a person to review.
purpose: Protects the fairness of the game. Flags are recorded for review only.
why: The header says flags are a stub: recorded for review and never acted on automatically.
how: lockAllowed compares the server time with the feed cutoff. anomalyFlags looks at lock times for bursts, runs of correct picks, and near-maximum confidence across many calls.
inputs: For a lock: server time, feed cutoff and mode. For flags: a list of calls with lock time, confidence as a fraction, and whether the call was correct.
outputs: Either allowed, or refused with a plain reason. A list of flags, each with a kind and a short detail.
risks: Flags are a stub and do not act. The lock check depends on the server clock being right. The thresholds are fixed guesses in code.
debug: If a lock is refused, compare the server time with the feed cutoff. If flags look wrong, check the confidence values, which are fractions from 0 to 1.
